$comment: Machine-readable OpenZeppelin -> XChain pattern-helper map. Lets tooling (docs, scaffolders, AI on-ramp) resolve a name a Solidity dev already knows to the paste-in helper(s) that cover it. Each helper MUST be a top-level function in the referenced file; patterns/oz-aliases.test.js enforces that. This is a naming index, not a drop-in shim: XChain contracts are single-file, import-free JS, so you paste the helpers, you do not import an OZ package.

aliases.note: Store the owner address under state key 'owner' in initialize(); onlyOwner(xchain) throws for non-owners.
No native two-step transfer helper; implement pending-owner in state and gate acceptance with onlyOwner on the pending key.
onlyRole(xchain, roleKey) gates to the address stored under roleKey (e.g. 'arbiter', 'minter'). Set roles in initialize().
Owner-controlled circuit breaker. Token-wide pause also exists natively via the SLEEP action.

Not needed. Emissions and emit.execute are deferred (applied after your method returns), so classic reentrancy is impossible by construction. Discipline that replaces nonReentrant: commit state BEFORE emitting (see state-machine.js + safe-transfer.js).
Size transfers from the contract's real holdings (getBalance), never from caller-supplied amounts; emit.send moves tokens via the audited protocol handler.
Use the built-in xchain.math.* bignumber API (add/subtract/multiply/divide/compare/gt/...). No overflow, and floats are rejected at deploy, so a dedicated library is unnecessary.
requireAddress(xchain, v, name) validates a non-empty address string up front.
Do not write a token contract. A fungible token is a first-class protocol object: ISSUE to create, SEND to transfer, balances are queryable directly.
No NFT contract needed. ISSUE with DECIMALS=0 and LOCK_MAX_SUPPLY=1 is a native non-fungible token.
Use a controller-bound token (ISSUE v6 binding a guard contract): the royalty/transfer rule is enforced by the protocol on every transfer and cannot be bypassed by a marketplace.
No set type; compose keys in the flat state store (e.g. state.set('member:'+addr,'1')). requireEnum validates a value against an allowed list.
